prereg.prediction: Every algebraic step of Jacobson 1995 closes in sympy: (S1) Raychaudhuri with theta(p)=sigma(p)=0 gives theta = -lambda R_kk + O(lambda^2); (S2) dQ = kappa eps^2 T_kk A/2, dA = eps^2 R_kk A/2; (S3) dQ = T eta dA with T = hbar kappa/2pi gives T_kk = (hbar eta/2pi) R_kk with kappa, eps, A cancelling; (S4) a symmetric M_ab with M_kk = 0 for every null k is f g_ab (solution space of dimension exactly 1); (S5) the contracted Bianchi identity div(G_ab + Lambda g_ab) = 0 holds identically on test metric families with arbitrary functions; (S6) conservation fixes f = -R/2 + Lambda; (S7) G_ab + Lambda g_ab = (2pi/hbar eta) T_ab and 8 pi G = 2pi/(hbar eta) gives eta = 1/(4 hbar G); (S8) the SI restoration is unique: eta = k_B c^3/(4 G hbar) = k_B/(4 l_P^2); (S9) EGJ shear: allowing sigma(p) != 0 gives a shear viscosity eta_s = hbar eta/(4 pi) = 1/(16 pi G), eta_s/s = hbar/(4 pi); (S10) Schwarzschild consistency: kappa = c^2/(2 r_s), T_H = hbar kappa/(2 pi c k_B), d(Mc^2) = T_H dS.

assumptions.text: [geometry input] Spacetime is a smooth 4-D Lorentzian manifold (signature -,+,+,+); at every point p a local inertial frame exists (equivalence principle), so g_ab = diag(-1,1,1,1) at p and local Rindler horizons can be built.

[construction] Local Rindler horizon: through p pick a small spacelike 2-surface P; its past-directed null normals generate a null congruence, affinely parametrised by lambda (lambda = 0 at p, lambda < 0 to the past), tangent k^a, hypersurface-orthogonal so the twist omega vanishes.

[construction, not a restriction on spacetime] P is chosen so that the expansion theta and the shear sigma of the inside congruence vanish at p. Jacobson 1995: 'It is always possible to choose P through p so that the expansion and shear vanish in a first order neighborhood of p.' Jacobson calls such a horizon 'instantaneously stationary (in local equilibrium) at p'; EGJ 2006 remark 4 later withdrew equilibrium as the reason for sigma(p) = 0 ('This is not valid however, since the shear defined with respect to Killing parameter would in any case vanish').

[physical assumption] Entropy is proportional to horizon area: dS = eta dA with eta a universal constant (motivated by vacuum entanglement across the horizon with a UV cutoff; eta is NOT fixed by the argument). With a non-constant entropy density (f(R)), EGJ show theta(p) != 0 is forced instead (S3b detail).

[QFT input] Unruh temperature: the vacuum seen by the boost observer is thermal at T = hbar kappa/(2 pi) (c = k_B = 1), kappa the acceleration of the orbit where |chi| = 1 (Unruh 1976; Bisognano-Wichmann).

[physical assumption] Heat = boost-energy flux of matter across the horizon: dQ = int_H T_ab chi^a dSigma^b with chi^a = -kappa lambda k^a (approximate boost Killing field vanishing at p) and dSigma^b = k^b dlambda dA. T_ab classical and symmetric; its quantum fluctuations are neglected. EGJ 2006 remark 5: the approximate Killing vector is ambiguous at O(x^3) while its lowest-order part is O(x), so the heat flux is fuzzy at relative order (patch size)^2/L_c^2.

[the postulate; carries the physics] The Clausius relation dQ = T dS holds as an EQUALITY (no internal entropy production) for every local Rindler horizon through every point p, i.e. for every null k, on horizons whose expansion and shear vanish at p (A3). theta(p) = 0 is also necessary for the equality (S3b, EGJ remark 4); sigma(p) = 0 is the condition for no internal entropy production (S3c, S9, EGJ remark 4).

[approximation] Leading order: the horizon patch is small compared with the curvature radius; R_kk and T_kk are evaluated at p and the relation is required only at the leading power of the patch size eps. It does NOT hold at the next order even with Einstein's equation imposed (diagnostic D1).
[physical assumption] Matter stress-energy is conserved: nabla^a T_ab = 0.
[topology] Spacetime (the domain of f) is connected, so a scalar with vanishing gradient is a constant.

[identification, not a prediction] The coupling 2 pi/(hbar eta) is NAMED 8 pi G with G taken from measurement; identifying the two gives eta = 1/(4 hbar G). eta (horizon entropy density) is not independently measured, so nothing is predicted.
[geometric identity] Raychaudhuri equation for an affinely parametrised null congruence: dtheta/dlambda = -theta^2/2 - sigma_ab sigma^ab + omega_ab omega^ab - R_ab k^a k^b.
[geometric identity, spot-checked in S5 and used live in S6] contracted Bianchi identity nabla^a (R_ab - R g_ab/2) = 0; metric compatibility nabla g = 0.

diagnostic_D1_next_order.what: next-order Clausius bookkeeping with Einstein's equation imposed along the whole generator
diagnostic_D1_next_order.reading: At leading order the gap is 0 (that is S3). At the next order it is -A R1 eta hbar kappa eps^3/(12 pi) even with Einstein's equation imposed along the generator; exact Clausius at O(eps^3) would need T1 = hbar eta R1/(4 pi), contradicting Einstein. Jacobson 1995 and EGJ 2006 claim the relation only at lowest order ('to lowest order in lambda', EGJ eq. 6), so this limits the scope of the statement and is not a defect of the argument. The largest neglected term is the gradient one, relative size eps R1/(3 R0), first order in eps; theta^2/2 is eps^2 R/12 and the Killing-vector fuzz eps^2/L_c^2.

S1, S1b, S4, S5, S6 do not use A5/A6 and close under both; their own live checks are the closed-form ODE, the S4 planar negative control and the S6 alpha solve. S3b closes under both because theta(p) = 0 is forced for any Unruh factor and either chi sign.
